summary:
ASTRO-TRAINER X is an interactive educational and robotics platform that merges space science with modern technologies. Leveraging NASA’s open-source data, it transforms complex space concepts into realistic scientific simulations, hands-on missions, and immersive learning experiences.
​The platform is designed to prepare and train the next generation of aspiring astronauts within a stimulating environment that blends innovation, experimentation, and scientific competition. It focuses on developing participants' core competencies across key domains, including space exploration, advanced programming, applied engineering, and complex problem-solving.
​By integrating interactive tools with practical applications, ASTRO-TRAINER X provides a comprehensive ecosystem where learners embark on unique exploratory journeys. Ultimately, it empowers youth to innovate and excel in the space and technology sectors, turning their passion for science into tangible, sustainable skills for the future.
details:
Here is the concise summary of ASTRO-TRAINER X focusing specifically on Programming Languages and Software/Tools in English:

​1. Programming Languages

​Python: Core backend language used for fetching NASA Open APIs, data processing, and AI terrain-recognition models.

​C++ / Arduino: Low-level firmware programming for microcontrollers, motor drivers, and real-time sensor processing on physical rovers.

​JavaScript (React / Node.js): Powers the web-based Mission Control dashboard, real-time telemetry charts, and interactive user interfaces.

​Blockly / Scratch (Visual Coding): Drag-and-drop visual coding blocks designed for younger students to learn autonomous navigation logic.

​2. Software, Simulation Engines & Middleware

​Unity 3D / Three.js (WebGL): 3D simulation engines used to render realistic lunar and Martian surface environments with accurate physics and lighting.

​ROS 2 (Robot Operating System): Middleware platform handling autonomous path planning, SLAM mapping, and sensor integration.

​MQTT / WebSockets: Low-latency communication protocols connecting the Mission Control interface to physical or simulated rovers.
